record.paper_title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
record.original_question: What is the smallest degree d such that Hilb_d(A^3) is reducible? The paper records the bounds 12 <= d <= 78.

evidence.quote: Problem V. What is the smallest d such that Hilbd(A^3) is reducible? We have 12 <= d <= 78.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3_k)$ denote the Hilbert scheme parametrizing zero-dimensional closed subschemes of length $d$ in affine $3$-space $\mathbb{A}^3_k$. It is known that $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3_k)$ is irreducible for all $d \le 11$, and that it is reducible for sufficiently large $d$ (in particular for some $d \le 78$). Determine the smallest positive integer $d$ for which $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3_k)$ is reducible.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact smallest value of $d$ for which $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3)$ becomes reducible is not known. Irreducibility is established up to $d=11$ (Douvropoulos–Jelisiejew–Nødland–Teitler, 2017), while reducibility is known for some specific values $\le 78$ (and classically for $d \ge 102$ via Iarrobino-style constructions). No improvement closing the gap appears in the literature, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Hilbert scheme of 11 points in A^3 is irreducible
status_evidence.snippet: The Hilbert scheme of 11 points on a smooth threefold is irreducible.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the lower bound: Hilb_d(A^3) is irreducible for d <= 11.

status_evidence.title: The Hilbert scheme of points on a threefold, I
status_evidence.snippet: Hilb_d is irreducible for d <= 11 but not for d >= 78.
status_evidence.claim: Upper bound on the smallest reducible d is 78; gap with lower bound 12 not closed.
